newsitem.title: DUBAI: Work starts on Saudi-Japan pharmaceutical plant.
newsitem.headline: Work starts on Saudi-Japan pharmaceutical plant.

text.p: A Saudi health official has laid the foundation stone of a 72 million riyal Saudi-Japanese joint venture pharmaceutical plant in Jeddah, a newspaper reported on Thursday.

The Arab News said the Saudi Arabian Japanese Pharmaceutical Co (Sajaphco) is a 51-49 percent joint venture between a Saudi company -- Farouk Maamoun Tamer Industries -- and a group of Japanese firms.
Sajaphco plans to start production by end-1998.
Japan International Development Organisation (JAIDO), Sankyo Co, Yamanouchi Pharmaceutical Co and Marubeni Corp are the Japanese partners.
The Japanese government owns 40 percent of JAIDO, which invests in and extends loans for projects which help stabilise economies in developing countries.
Saudi Arabia is one of the Middle East's top pharmaceutical consumers, with the market valued at more than three billion riyals annually, of which local production accounts for less than 15 percent.
